content: Methylodopa and hydrochlorothiazide are prescribed together to manage high blood pressure. Methylodopa functions by relaxing blood vessels, which allows blood to flow more easily throughout the body. Hydrochlorothiazide helps reduce blood pressure by removing excess water and salt from the body. This medication may also be prescribed for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. This medication is available in tablet form and is taken orally, typically two or three times a day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take methylodopa and hydrochlorothiazide exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it or take it more frequently than prescribed. This medication helps control high blood pressure but does not cure it. Continue taking it even if you feel well, and do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor. Before taking methylodopa and hydrochlorothiazide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to methylodopa, hydrochlorothiazide, sulfa drugs, or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially cholestyramine (Questran), digoxin (Lanoxin), haloperidol (Haldol), levodopa (Sinemet), lithium (Lithobid, Eskalith), MAO inhibitors, diabetes medications, prednisone (Deltasone), probenecid (Benemid), tolbutamide (Orinase), and vitamins. Avoid taking this medication with iron supplements or vitamins containing iron. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had kidney or liver disease, diabetes, gout, or high blood cholesterol. Notify your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking this medication, contact your doctor immediately. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental surgery, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking methylodopa and hydrochlorothiazide. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating machinery for 48–72 hours after starting this medication or after a dose increase. Consult your doctor about the safe use of alcohol while taking this medication, as alcohol can exacerbate its side effects. Your doctor may recommend a low-salt or low-sodium diet. Follow these dietary instructions carefully. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Methylodopa and hydrochlorothiazide may cause side effects. A harmless effect is the darkening of urine when exposed to air. Notify your doctor if any of the following symptoms are severe or persistent: frequent urination, dry mouth, drowsiness, headache, upset stomach, vomiting, loss of appetite, diarrhea, gas, or rash. If you experience any of the following severe symptoms, contact your doctor immediately: extreme tiredness, muscle weakness or cramps, unexplained fever, yellowing of the skin or eyes, difficulty breathing, or swelling of the ankles or feet. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory for regular blood pressure monitoring to assess your response to the medication. To alleviate dry mouth caused by this medication, chew gum or suck on sugarless hard candy. Do not share your medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
